headline: High-risk default workspace overlap: CrewAI can write/read the host working directory while Cognee handles sensitive support data, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI reads and writes the host working directory and uses stdin/stdout, so it can ingest Cognee-produced files or outputs if wired together. Cognee handles documents and support history, which could contain attacker-controlled content. No shared channel is explicit, so this is an inferred default-pathway risk rather than a proven one.
conditions: IF CrewAI is configured to consume files or stdout produced by Cognee
IF Cognee writes user-supplied documents into a shared directory readable by CrewAI
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable file-based handoff between agents
Add a content-sanitization step before CrewAI reads Cognee output
Use explicit provenance tags on all shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add a broker that strips instructions from untrusted text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee touches personal data, finance data, and support history, while CrewAI has broad network egress and can read the host filesystem. If they share a workspace, CrewAI can exfiltrate sensitive files to model providers or tools. The pair lacks default isolation on CrewAI, so the blast radius includes sensitive-data leakage.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or working directory
IF CrewAI is configured with tools that transmit file contents to external services
mitigations: Place Cognee and CrewAI in separate containers
Restrict CrewAI to a non-sensitive mount
Remove sensitive files from the shared workspace
Turn off any tool that uploads file contents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can operate on the same host workspace: Cognee supports multiple instances with session memory, and CrewAI can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses. Even without git writes, concurrent edits to shared files or artifacts can overwrite each other. The conflict is plausible in default deployments that reuse a directory.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory
IF either agent writes intermediate artifacts without locking
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Serialize write operations between agents
Keep CrewAI subprocess outputs in a temp directory
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI is a multi-agent orchestrator with shared memory, so it may treat Cognee outputs as authoritative inputs. Cognee produces decisions, workflows, and schema structures, which CrewAI could then act on without verification. That creates a default-pathway cascade from one agent's generated content into another agent's actions.
conditions: IF CrewAI agents consume Cognee-generated text as task context
IF no verification or human review step is inserted before downstream actions
mitigations: Require a human review gate for high-impact actions
Add schema validation to Cognee outputs before CrewAI uses them
Mark Cognee outputs as untrusted by default
Limit CrewAI tools to read-only during initial runs
requires-engineering: implement citation/provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and can send it to model providers or tools. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Uncertainty pushes this above low because sensitive data classes are involved.
conditions: IF personal data or finance data is passed from Cognee into CrewAI tools or model providers
IF the deployment lacks a documented DPA, retention policy, or residency control
mitigations: Document the data classes shared between agents
Block finance or personal data from CrewAI inputs
Review provider retention settings
Add a residency check before external calls
requires-engineering: align both agents to the same compliance boundary
